html:
Mennonites settled in Belize from 1958, when German-speaking farmers moved there from Mexico and Canada. They founded farming colonies such as Spanish Lookout and Blue Creek.

The Mennonites are Protestant Christians who refuse military service and keep apart from the wider world. Their ancestors had left Russia for Canada and then Canada for Mexico, always in search of freedom to run their own schools. The government of British Honduras gave them land and that freedom in return for farming the interior.

They cleared forest and built up dairy, poultry, grain and furniture making. Today they supply much of the country's milk, eggs and chicken. Some colonies use tractors and electricity; others still farm with horses. They are one of the many peoples of Belize.
